title: PebbleBank KYC onramp scratchpad
content:
Meeting: 2025-10-28 — Kickoff with PebbleBank (Sasha - Head of Risk, Omar - Infra PM)

Quick context:
- PebbleBank: mid-sized neobank focusing on US + UK customers. Heavy AML/KYC requirements for higher-risk cohorts.
- Goal: add an assistant to triage KYC docs and answer agent questions; accelerate manual review but preserve audit trail.
- Want to evaluate Redwood hosted API first, then move to Private (VPC) for production.

Call notes / requirements (raw):
- Data residency: UK customers' PII must remain in EU region. Legal wants confirmation of KMS/HSM separation for keys.
- VPC requirement for production (private control plane preferred) — must support peered VPC with strict egress rules.
- Retention: bank wants 7-day cache TTL for KV prefix cache, but logs/audit must be retained 3 years (we need to clarify what they mean by logs vs transcripts).
- Redaction: must avoid model seeing full PANs / SSNs. They will pre-redact but want our guidance on redaction pipeline and detection (PII regex + fuzzy detect).
- Throughput: expected 800 agents/day, 6k doc uploads/month. Peak concurrent reviewers: ~12. Target p95 latency for short lookups < 400ms (for text-chat queries).
- File types: PDFs (scans), PNG/JPEG images (ID photos). Need OCR pipeline and a module to strip bad OCR output.
- Embeddings: they want semantic search over docs for context retrieval. Concerned about embedding drift and storage costs.
- Model behavior: want deterministic extraction for structured fields (name, DOB, doc type). Prefer function-calling / structured output.

Gotchas / unknowns to resolve:
- OCR quality: scanned PDFs from branch offices are low res. We should propose Tesseract + simple cleanup, but may suggest vendor OCR if accuracy too low. Need sample PDFs. ACTION: ask client to share 20 representative redacted PDFs. (Owner: Liam, due 2025-11-04)
- Cost sensitivity: finance asked about cost per 1k KYC queries. Need to model hosted vs dedicated vs private. Quick guesstimate: hosted API with batching & caching should be cheapest for prototyping; Dedicated reserved capacity for prod if sustained throughput.
- PII handling path: unclear whether they want us to store raw uploads in S3 in their account (recommended) or our bucket. Prefer customer-managed S3. ACTION: confirm storage model with Omar (Owner: Priya, due 2025-11-06).
- Audit log format: they want signed, tamper-evident logs. Our console supports audit export but need to confirm schema & signing (HSM). ACTION: check with security (Rafael) on supported signing workflows (Owner: Rafael, due 2025-11-05).
- Model selection: they asked about small vs large models for extraction. Recommendation: use a smaller extraction model (quantized) for structured field extraction, reserve larger LLM for free-text assistant responses. ACTION: draft model/quantization recommendation doc (Owner: Maya, due 2025-11-07).

Technical notes / architecture sketch (brain dump):
- Ingest: S3 (customer) -> Lambda (or small runner) triggers -> OCR -> text normalization -> store raw + parsed text in secure bucket, generate embeddings for doc chunks -> upsert to vector DB (their VPC if private)
- Retrieval: request hits Redwood route -> route policy: first check prefix cache for doc-level keys -> if miss, retrieve doc chunks + embeddings from vector DB -> build context (limit tokens) -> call extraction model via Redwood runtime (structured output) -> return to reviewer UI
- Caching: prefix/KV cache for recently-accessed customer docs (TTL 7 days as requested). Need cache eviction policy for multi-tenant clusters; propose per-customer namespaces.
- Batching: group small extraction tasks (like NER) into micro-batches to improve GPU utilization but ensure latency SLO for interactive review. Suggest dynamic batching with cap 100ms assembly window.

Security / compliance notes:
- KMS: must support customer-managed keys in cloud KMS (AWS KMS) and optional HSM-backed signing. Put this in SOW if they move to Private.
- Network: VPC peering + strict egress to S3 endpoints. No public egress for production.
- Data minimization: advise storing only redacted transcripts in Redwood logs; raw uploads remain in customer S3.

Immediate action items (compact):
- Ask PebbleBank for sample PDFs (20) + list of doc types + sample redaction policy (Owner: Liam O'Connor, due 2025-11-04).
- Confirm storage model and S3 account access pattern (Owner: Priya Desai, due 2025-11-06).
- Security: confirm audit signing & HSM support for Private (Owner: Rafael Gomez, due 2025-11-05).
- Product: draft quick config templates for KYC pipeline in Console (route, model profile, cache TTLs) — attach to PE-1137 (Owner: Maya Chen, due 2025-11-07).
- Finance: prepare cost comparison table hosted vs dedicated vs private for expected qps (Owner: Maya + Finance, due 2025-11-10).

Open questions to raise on next call:
1) Do they need synchronous extraction for agent flows, or is async ok and results posted back to a ticket? (Operational impact on latency)
2) Legal wants to see our data deletion SOP for test/dev data — can we share redacted SOP or is an NDA required?
3) Which region(s) should we prioritize for EU residency? (EU-West-1 vs EU-West-3?)
4) Are there pre-existing connectors to their case management system (we saw they use CaseFlow v2) — need API doc.

Notes to self:
- Keep recommendations pragmatic: start hosted with strict RBAC + S3 customer-managed storage for rapid proof-of-concept, then transition to Private with HSM if they sign an enterprise contract.
- Emphasize controllable cost levers: caching TTLs, batch windows, quantized extraction models, chunk size for embeddings.
- Watch out for hallucination when extracting structured fields from noisy OCR — add verification step in UI (highlight extracted field + confidence).

Next sync: scheduled 2025-11-06 with Sasha (30min) — agenda: sample PDFs review, confirm storage choice, agree pilot timeline.

Raw timeline (very rough):
- Week 0 (now): get samples + legal constraints documented.
- Week 1: prototype OCR + extraction on samples, initial cost estimate.
- Week 2-3: small pilot (hosted) with 2 reviewers, measure p95 latency & accuracy.
- Week 4+: iterate or plan Dedicated/Private rollout based on results.

Misc shorthand / scratch:
- Quick grep: check existing connector code under github repo "pebblebank-connector" (PR 12 has S3 hookup).
- Potential blocker: branch office scanned docs might require manual pre-clean step -> might push them to vendor OCR. Note in PM backlog.

End of notes.
